A_target.statement:
In the [[Definition:Simply Typed Lambda Calculus|simply typed $\lambda$-calculus]] with products, the terms:
:$\mathsf {curry} = \lambda f. \lambda a. \lambda b. f \tuple {a, b}, \quad \mathsf {uncurry} = \lambda g. \lambda p. g \paren {\pi_1 p} \paren {\pi_2 p}$
are mutually inverse up to $\beta \eta$-equality, so $\paren {A \times B \to C} \cong \paren {A \to B \to C}$.

B_source.statement:
In a [[Definition:Cartesian Closed Category|cartesian closed category]] there is a bijection, natural in $X$:
:$\map {\operatorname {Hom} } {X \times A, B} \cong \map {\operatorname {Hom} } {X, B^A}$

object_map.reformulation: Transport the defining adjunction of exponentials into the term calculus, where it becomes beta-eta laws.

validity_conditions: The eta-rules for products and functions are needed for the composites to be identities.
Naturality in X corresponds to compatibility with substitution of contexts.
proof_plan: Read types as objects, terms in context as morphisms, $\times$ as the product and $\to$ as the exponential.
$\map {\mathsf {uncurry} } {\map {\mathsf {curry} } f} \twoheadrightarrow_\beta \lambda p. f \tuple {\pi_1 p, \pi_2 p}$, which is $\eta$-equal to $f$, using surjective pairing.
$\map {\mathsf {curry} } {\map {\mathsf {uncurry} } g} \twoheadrightarrow_\beta \lambda a. \lambda b. g \, a \, b$, which is $\eta$-equal to $g$.
